context: Request: the firm's first traditional, non-SPAC IPO, with its offering documents and a document showing the deal closed. Rubric: 1037-00001 (Solstice Biomedical ADS IPO, closed March 2023), an offering document from it (underwriting, registration-rights or lock-up agreement), a closing deliverable (checklist, officers' or secretary's certificate), and a precision criterion; 1010-00002 (Arbor Health, 2024) is outside the set.

runs.failure_point: The answer's comparison section calls a later candidate a completed offering of the requested kind, which was read as asserting a second qualifying matter.

first_error.critic_note: Reviews only repeated stock advice not to add or drop matters; none named the comparator described as qualifying.
first_error.why: The comparison section describes a later candidate as a completed offering of the requested kind, which the precision check read as a second qualifying matter (evidence seen at [56]-[70]); T0 used almost the same wording and passed.

divergence: Mixed (T0, T1 pass; T2 fails the precision criterion only). All three runs settled on the same matter from file-name sweeps and reads, and cited the same offering and closing documents. They split at the write stage: T1 left the later completed candidate out of its answer, T0 and T2 both described it as a completed offering of the same kind that closed later; the judge accepted this in T0 and counted it as qualifying in T2. The write and check reviews did not differ in a relevant way: in all runs they gave the stock advice not to add or drop matters and named no comparator.
